gaps.quote: It permutes the coefficients and changes some signs, so it is a linear-time pass over the list.
gaps.note: Does not follow as stated: an arbitrary signed permutation of a list on a tape is not a linear-time pass. It is linear only because multiplication by y^a is a rotation, i.e. the list is split into two pieces that are swapped, with the moved piece negated and a common sign applied (paper line 3148-3156, cost O(rp) per record). The page never gives this two-piece structure, so the reader cannot check the claim.
